name: Densest Subgraph (twice)
definition: The **densest subgraph dimension** of a concept class is equal to twice the density of the densest subgraph (a.k.a. **subgraph density**) of its $1$-inclusion graph.
graph_summary: Twice the maximum edge density of an induced subgraph of the one-inclusion graph.
origin_references: The density and densest-subgraph treatment of the $1$-inclusion graph is part of the random-point prediction framework developed in \cite{haussler1988predicting,haussler1994predicting}.
comments: The densest subgraph is dual to the lowest outdegree orientation. Conditioning gives an induced subgraph of the $1$-inclusion graph, so this parameter is c-monotonic.

monotonic.proof: The 1-inclusion graph of a subfamily is an induced subgraph of the original graph. Every subgraph considered in the densest-subgraph maximum for the subfamily is therefore also a subgraph considered for the original class.

c_monotonic.proof: Conditioning gives an induced subgraph of the one-inclusion graph.  The maximum subgraph density cannot increase on an induced subgraph.

p_monotonic.proof: Counterexample: $\mathcal H=\{000,001,110\}$ has a single one-inclusion edge, hence densest-subgraph value 1. Projecting to the last two coordinates gives $\{00,01,10\}$, a two-edge path whose doubled density is $4/3$.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, doubly monotonicity requires both subfamily monotonicity and projection monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

strictly_monotonic.proof: By definition, strictly monotonicity requires both doubly monotonicity and strict c-monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.
